symptom: pip or npm install times out or cannot download packages
steps: Check your internet works by opening any website.
If you are on campus Wi-Fi or a VPN, try another network such as a phone hotspot.
If your network uses a proxy, set it in your terminal before installing.
Retry with a longer timeout, for example 'pip install --timeout 60 <package>'.
Check your computer's date and time are correct, because certificates depend on them.
Update the certificate bundle with 'pip install --upgrade pip certifi'.
On a work or school network, ask IT for their security certificate and install it.
Do not switch off SSL checking to make the error go away.

symptom: Connection timed out when opening my cloud server
steps: Check the server is running and you are using its current public IP address, because it can change after a restart.
Check the firewall or AWS security group allows the port you are using.
Check the app on the server listens on 0.0.0.0, not just 127.0.0.1.
Test from the server itself with 'curl localhost:<port>' to see if the app answers there.

symptom: Website name cannot be found (DNS error)
steps: Check the address is spelled correctly.
Run 'nslookup <name>' to see if the name turns into an IP address.
Clear the DNS cache with 'ipconfig /flushdns' on Windows.
Try a public DNS server such as 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 in your network settings.

symptom: My app does not pick up a setting from the .env file
steps: Check the setting's name is spelled exactly the same in the code and in the .env file.
Check the .env file is in the folder the app starts from (for Docker Compose, next to compose.yaml).
Restart the app after changing .env, because settings are only read when it starts.
Print the setting when the app starts to confirm it was loaded, but never print passwords.
